angle: The biggest ROI from AI comes from slashing decision latency, not headcount.
sourceTitle: The decision dividend: How AI creates economic value
linkedinPost:
Most AI business cases I see are built on the wrong line of the P&L.

A recent piece from McKinsey argues the largest AI gains come from faster decisions, better asset use, and catching opportunities you’d otherwise miss—not from labor savings alone.

That matches what I see on the ground. A claims team that cuts “time to decision” from 3 days to 30 minutes unlocks cash and customer trust. A field ops group that routes parts proactively squeezes more out of the same trucks and techs. No layoffs required.

If your AI ROI hinges on FTE reduction, you’re likely under-scoping the real value. Shift the scorecard:
- Decision cycle time (before/after)
- First-pass yield / rework rate
- Asset utilization (trucks, rooms, inventory)
- Opportunity capture (upsell, win rate) tied to AI suggestions actually used

Also: measure adoption like a product team. If users aren’t acting on the AI’s recommendations, there is no “decision dividend.”

My take: Put “decision latency” on the exec dashboard and fund the boring workflow plumbing that shortens it. That’s where returns show up.

What’s one decision your org could speed up by 10x with AI today? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy
